extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages designed to evaluate computational models on a word prediction task that requires understanding of a broad discourse context rather than just a local sentence.
extraction.creator: Denis Papemo, Germ ´an Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Phamy, Raffaella Bemardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fem ´andezz
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by extracting narrative passages from novels and filtering them based on the ability of human subjects to guess the final word when given the broad context versus only the local sentence context.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Narrative passages extracted from a corpus of novels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A three-step crowdsourcing process was used where subjects had to guess the missing target word. In step 1, one subject guessed based on the whole passage. If correct, step 2 required a second subject to also guess correctly based on the whole passage. In step 3, up to 10 subjects attempted to guess the word using only the target sentence (up to 3 guesses each). Passages were only included if no subject in step 3 could guess the word.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors analyzed the discard rates at each step of the annotation pipeline, noting that the strict exact-match criteria resulted in only about 1 in 25 examples passing all selection steps.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 12 annotations per included item (2 subjects evaluating the whole passage, and 10 subjects evaluating the target sentence only).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset contains a strong part-of-speech distribution bias, where proper nouns are heavily over-represented and other categories like verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are under-represented or rare.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to evaluate and test computational models for text understanding through a word prediction task. It provides specific splits for training, development, and testing language models.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development set and training corpus are hosted at a specific URL for download, while the test set was planned to be released later during a public competition.

name.evidence: We introduce LAMBADA, a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task.

description.evidence: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we extracted from the training novels similar-shaped passages to those in LAMBADA

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: we extracted from the training novels similar-shaped passages to those in LAMBADA

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: For a given passage, 1. one human subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; if the guess was right, 2. a second subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; if that guess was also right, 3. more subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only, until the word was guessed or the number of unsuccessful guesses reached 10; if no subject was able to guess the target word, the passage was added to the LAMBADA dataset.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: ...evaluated by human subjects through the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service...

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: In the crowdsourcing pipeline, 84–86% items were discarded at step 1, an additional 6–7% at step 2 and another 3–5% at step 3. Only about one in 25 input examples passed all the selection steps.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: 1. one human subject guessed the target word... 2. a second subject guessed the target word... 3. more subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only, until the word was guessed or the number of unsuccessful guesses reached 10; if no subject was able to guess the target word, the passage was added to the LAMBADA dataset.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: proper nouns are hugely over-represented in LAMBADA, while the other categories are under-represented, compared to the POS distribution in the input.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We introduce LAMBADA, a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. [...] The LAMBADA dataset consists of 10,022 passages, divided into 4,869 development and 5,153 test passages

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The development set of LAMBADA, along with the training corpus, can be downloaded at http://clic.cimec.unitn.it/lambada/. The test set will be made available at the time of the competition.
